claim_results.reason: All 16 supplied review tests passed. Inspection and execution confirmed consumption-time packet validation, unique obligations, content-addressed identity, immutable reviewer binding, recursive duplicate-key rejection, and invalidation by changed inputs or snapshots. Additional independent tests confirmed that negative and incomplete reviews remain negative and cannot be overwritten, missing completion cannot produce a receipt, and identical retries recover injected publication failures. Actual child-process exits after identity, spawn, dispatch, completion, report and receipt publication also recovered after confirming termination and preserving the stale lock. No remaining actionable defect was found within the documented trusted-coordinator boundary.

All 80 supplied tests passed, including 37 correction, 16 library, 16 review and 11 experience tests. The current CL1–CL5 repairs passed their reproductions: committed membership/head checks detect trailing deletion; opaque indexing blocks IncludeUnreviewed bypass; persisted registration intent supports crash recovery while rejecting corruption; conflicting aliases are rejected; and the documented manual opaque repair works with the stated save_card limitation. Additional independent checks confirmed exact legacy-adoption expectations, preservation of immutable bytes, custom-root operation, dependency/receipt invalidation and unchanged canonical sentinels. However, an upstream-only release reproducibly cleared unchanged downstream cards without their own repair or review, contrary to the declared release scope.

findings.problem: Releasing an upstream candidate can silently clear previously affected downstream versions. impact_states removes released versions from the blocked set and skips them during propagation, then recomputes downstream state without retaining the downstream review obligation. This contradicts v2-corrections.md lines 246–248, which require separate repair and review of affected downstream cards.
findings.reproduction: Created upstream versions A0 and A1, with A1 an existing repair; created B depending exactly on A1 and C depending exactly on B. Quarantined A1 through the documented preexisting-repair workflow. B and C became needs_review and disappeared from ordinary retrieval. Proposed A0-to-A1, created an explicitly synthetic receipt covering only that repair, and released A1. Both unchanged downstream versions became clear with reuse_allowed=true, returned through default query with ordinary retrieval trust, and reappeared in active index items. The journal contained only one issue, one upstream revision and one upstream release; neither downstream card had a repair or review. This was reproduced twice, including a failing independent regression test.
findings.requested_change: Preserve the issue obligation for each previously affected downstream version until its own scoped repair and review release succeeds. Add regression coverage for direct and transitive dependents of a quarantined preexisting repair, asserting that an upstream-only release cannot reopen them.

limitations: Receipt tests used explicitly synthetic transcripts. They establish software behavior, not live service authenticity, actual context isolation, completeness of author disclosure or OS attestation.

Execution used disposable Linux filesystem projects, injected failures, actual process exits and supplied concurrent-writer tests. Power-loss durability, Windows filesystem behavior and exhaustive concurrency interleavings were not verified.
The review evaluated software obligations. Mathematical fixtures and successful tests do not establish mathematical correctness, universal claims or complete formalization.

Only the frozen packet and its 12 listed snapshots were inspected. Live project state was not compared. The source project was not modified, and final hashes of the packet and every listed snapshot still matched the manifest.
